newsitem.title: UAE: Saudi captain of crashed plane buried.
newsitem.headline: Saudi captain of crashed plane buried.

text.p: The Saudi pilot in the world's worst mid-air collision was buried in the Moslem holy city of Medina in Saudi Arabia on Saturday, Gulf news agencies said.

Distraught relatives of 45-year-old Khalid al-Shubaily, whose body was flown to Saudi Arabia after his brother identified it near the crash site in India, attended the funeral in the city, home to one of Islam's holiest shrines.
Majdi Akroubi, the only Saudi passenger in Tuesday's accident involving a Saudi Arabian jumbo jet and a Kazakh plane, was also laid to rest in Medina in line with his will, the agencies added.
Saudi Arabia was working with embassies to hand over the remains of non-Saudi crew members killed in the collision, the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA) reported.
"We are working with embasssies and relatives of non-Saudi crew members to hand over their bodies," SPA quoted Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp director-general Khaled Ben-Bakr as saying.
The remains of 14 crew members, including four anti-terrorism security men, and one Saudi passenger arrived in Saudi on Friday on a special Jeddah-bound flight from New Delhi.
Rescue teams were still looking for the body of the fifth security officer.
The remains of the crew members include those of two Moroccans, a Jordanian, an Algerian, a Tunisian and nine Saudis, SPA added.

The Saudi airliner with 312 people on board and a KazAir Ilyushin IL-76 freighter carrying 37 collided in flight seven minutes after the Saudi plane had taken off from New Delhi. There were no survivors.
